entry.name: mtr
entry.description: Records messages and provides sequenced playback.

arguments.name: tracks
arguments.description: Specifies the number of tracks in. The number of tracks determines the number of inlets and outlets in addition to the leftmost inlet and outlet. Up to 128 tracks are possible. If there is no argument, there will only be one track.

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: autostart
attributes.digest: Play tracks when transport is started
attributes.description: Sets whether mtr plays all tracks when the transport is started. Default is 0 (off). This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: autostarttime
attributes.digest: Autostart Time
attributes.description: Sets the autostarttime for mtr. If theattribute is enabled,will play all tracks automatically at the time specified with this attribute.can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: bindto
attributes.digest: Bind objects to tracks
attributes.description: Bind individual UI objects to tracks without patch cords using pattr scripting names. If you assign a scripting name to a UI object, you can use that same name to set bindings to. The typed in arguments for @bindto should be the track number followed by the scripting name of the desired object.

attributes.name: color
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: embed
attributes.digest: Save Data with Patcher
attributes.description: Whenis set to 1, any recorded data is saved with the patcher. Note that recording, changing, or clearing data does not cause the patcher to be dirtied. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: fontface
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontsize
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: hidden
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: hint
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: ignoreclick
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: jspainterfile
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: length
attributes.digest: Length of tracks
attributes.description: Sets the length of all tracks in time units. This defines when the track will stop or loop. If the length is shorter than the original recorded length, events after the specified time are not played but are still present in the track. This attribute can be set via the inspector, attrui, as a typed-in argument, or as a message to the left inlet. When set this way,is considered a global attribute and will overwrite any previously set track-specific length values.If sent as a message to any non-left inlet, it sets the length of the track in time units that corresponds to the inlet. If a length value is subsequently set globally (see above), all track-specific values are overwritten.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.digest: Loop tracks
attributes.description: Turns looping off/on for all tracks. This attribute can be set via the inspector, attrui, as a typed-in argument, or as a message to the left inlet. When set this way,is considered a global attribute and will overwrite any previously set track-specific loop values.If sent as a message to any non-left inlet, it sets the looping state of the track that corresponds to the inlet. If thevalue is subsequently set globally (see above), all track-specific values are overwritten.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Automation playback mode
attributes.description: Enables automation playback mode, which when starting or restarting a track will play the last event before the(if a selection start point is non-zero). The default value is 0 (off). This attribute can be set via the inspector, attrui, as a typed-in argument, or as a message to the left inlet. When set this way,is considered a global attribute and will overwrite any track-specific settings that were previously specified.If sent as a message to any non-left inlet, it enables/disables automation playback mode for the track that corresponds to the inlet. If theattribute is subsequently set globally (see above), all track-specific settings are overwritten.

attributes.name: nextmode
attributes.digest: next message behavior
attributes.description: Sets how themessage behaves. Whenis set to 0, amessage after the last event will produce an event with a delta time of -1. Whenis set to 1 (loop mode), amessage after the last event will immediately loop back to the first event. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: patching_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: position
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: quantize
attributes.digest: Sets playback quantization
attributes.description: Sets playback quantization. This does not change the actual events in tracks, only how they are played. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: selection
attributes.digest: Playback selection of tracks
attributes.description: Sets the playback selection of all tracks. The selection is made in normalized units based on the length of the track, either defined via theattribute, or if length is 0, the total recorded time. For example, "selection 0.25 0.75" will play the middle section of a track. When sending amessage to a track, it will start at the selection point, not the beginning. Playback is (subtly) affected by theattribute.This attribute can be set via the inspector, attrui, as a typed-in argument, or as a message to the left inlet. When set this way,is considered a global attribute and will overwrite any previously set track-specific selection values.If sent as a message to any non-left inlet, it sets the playback selection of the track that corresponds to the inlet. If theattribute is subsequently set globally (see above), all track-specific values are overwritten.

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: speed
attributes.digest: Speed Factor of all tracks
attributes.description: Sets the global multiplier to be applied to the speed of all tracks, where 1.0 is the original speed. This allows you to have individual tracks running at differents, and then apply a global speed change. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: sync
attributes.digest: Sync to Transport
attributes.description: Whenis enabled,syncs to a named transport (“internal” is the default). Whenis off, time units are in milliseconds. Whenis on, time units are in ticks. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: textjustification
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: trackspeed
attributes.digest: Speed of tracks
attributes.description: Sets the speed of all tracks, with 1.0 being the originally recorded speed. The actual track speed is a combination of the mtr'sattribute, the, and the. This attribute can be set via the inspector, attrui, as a typed-in argument, or as a message to the left inlet. When set this way,is considered a global attribute and will overwrite any previously set track-specific trackspeed values.If sent as a message to any non-left inlet, it sets the speed of the track that corresponds to the inlet. If a trackspeed value is subsequently set globally (see above), all track-specific values are overwritten.

attributes.name: transport
attributes.digest: Sets the transport name
attributes.description: Sets the transport name. The default setting is "internal", which is the global transport. This attribute can only be set globally, and does not apply to individual tracks.

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

messages.name: addevent
messages.digest: Add an event at a specific time
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list, absolute time and data, adds an event to a track at a specific time. For example, the message "addevent 1000 1" will add the event 1 at time 1000. This message can be sent while a track is recording, playing, or stopped. The message will only work in track-specific inlets, and cannot be sent to the left inlet.

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: Store the message on a track
messages.description: In any inlet other than the left inlet: If the track is currently being recorded, symbols received in that track's inlet are stored in, preceded by the delta time (the amount of time elapsed since the previous event).Althoughcan record individual bytes of MIDI messages received from, it stores each byte with a separate delta time, and does not format the MIDI messages the waydoes. If you want to record complete MIDI messages and edit them later,is better suited for the task. On the other hand,is perfectly suited for recording sequences of numbers, lists, or symbols from virtually any object in Max: specialized MIDI objects such asor, user interface objects such as,, and, or any other object.In order for a file to be read intofor playback, it must be in the proper format. Anmulti-track sequence can even be typed in a text file, provided it adheres to the format. The contents of the different tracks are listed in order in anfile, and the format of each track is as follows. Note that a semicolon () ends each line.Line 1:(Track in which to store subsequent data)Line 2, etc.:Last line:(End of this track's data)

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Send dictionary data out left outlet
messages.description: Just like themessage, sending ato the left inlet of, results in a dictionary being sent out the left outlet with information about the current state of the object. Both global and track specific informtion is included in the dictionary. An entry that begins with "global_" is the global setting for the specified attribute. If the same attribute has a track specific setting, that value will be listed under the track information.

messages.name: clear
messages.digest: Clear the contents of tracks
messages.description: In left inlet: Erases the contents of. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, clears those tracks.In other inlets: Erases the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: cleareventat
messages.digest: Clear an event at a specific time
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list, absolute time and matching criteria, clears all events that exactly match the criteria at the specific time. Unlike,does not delete the time occupied by the event. For example, if events are at time 1000, 2000, and 3000, and the event at 2000 is cleared, the next event remains at time 3000. This message can be sent while a track is recording, playing, or stopped. The message will only work in track-specific inlets, and cannot be sent to the left inlet.

messages.name: definelengthandstop
messages.digest: Stop recording and set track length
messages.description: In left inlet: Stops recording and sets the track’s length to the current recording time. Themessage, by contrast, does not set the track’s length; the total recorded length (available in the info dictionary) is defined by both messages and consists of the time between the start of the recording and the time of the final event recorded beforeoris received. The word, followed by one or more tracks, stops and sets the length for those tracks.In other inlets: Stops and sets the length of the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: delay
messages.digest: Set an initial delta time value
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, sets the first delta time value of each track to that number, so that all tracks begin playing back that amount of time after themessage is received.In other inlets: Sets the initial delta time of the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: deleteeventat
messages.digest: Delete an event at a specific time
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list, absolute time and matching criteria, deletes all events that exactly match the criteria at the specific time. The time occupied by the event is also deleted. "deleteeventat 1000" will delete all events at absolute time 1000 in the track. The message "deleteeventat 1000 3" will delete an event at absolute time 1000 containing 3. The event "3 4 5" will not be deleted because it does not match exactly. This message can be sent while a track is recording, playing, or stopped. The message will only work in track-specific inlets, and cannot be sent to the left inlet.

messages.name: dictionary
messages.digest: Send a dictionary to
messages.description: The message, followed by a name, will load that specific dictionary into, including all events from each track sequence.

messages.name: dump
messages.digest: Send dictionary data out left outlet
messages.description: The message, when sent to any inlet of, sends a dictionary out the left outlet of. Unlike the dictionary sent out from theormessages, this dictionary contains individual events from each track sequence.

messages.name: first
messages.digest: Set playback wait time
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, causesto wait that amount of time after amessage is received before playing back. Unlike,does not alter the delta time value of the first event in a track, it just waits a certain time (in addition to the first delta time) before playing back from the beginning.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Store the message on a track
messages.description: In any inlet other than the left inlet: If the track is currently being recorded, numbers received in that track's inlet are combined with a delta time (the amount of time elapsed since the previous event) and stored in.

messages.name: info
messages.digest: Send dictionary data out left outlet
messages.description: Just like, sending themessage to the left inlet of, results in a dictionary being sent out the left outlet with information about the current state of the object. Both global and track specific informtion is included in the dictionary. An entry that begins with "global_" is the global setting for the specified attribute. If the same attribute has a track specific setting, that value will be listed under the track information.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Store the message on a track
messages.description: In any inlet other than the left inlet: If the track is currently being recorded, numbers received in that track's inlet are combined with a delta time (the amount of time elapsed since the previous event) and stored in.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Store the message on a track
messages.description: In any inlet other than the left inlet: If the track is currently being recorded, lists received in that track's inlet are stored in, preceded by the delta time (the amount of time elapsed since the previous event). The maximum allowed length for a list is 4096 items.

messages.name: mute
messages.digest: Mute output
messages.description: In left inlet: Causesto stop producing output, while still continuing to "play" (still moving forward in the sequence). The word, followed by one or more tracks, mutes those tracks.In other inlets: Mutes the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: next
messages.digest: Output the next message
messages.description: In left inlet: Causes each track to output only the next message in its recorded sequence. When amessage is received, the track number, delta time, and absolute time of each message being output are sent out the leftmost outlet as a list. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, outputs the next message stored in those tracks.In other inlets: Outputs the next message stored on the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: play
messages.digest: Play back messages at their normal rate
messages.description: In left inlet: Plays back all messages recorded earlier, sending them out the corresponding outlets in the same rhythm and at the same speed they were recorded. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, begins playing those tracks.In other inlets: Plays back all messages on the track that corresponds to the inlet. When themessage is sent to specific track inlets you can give it two optional arguments: number of iterations and timescale. 100 is the original timescale. The message "play 3 200" will play the track three times, at twice the speed.

messages.name: playat
messages.digest: Start playback at a specific point (0-1)
messages.description: In left inlet: Starts playback of all messages at a specific point, which is specified in a normalized range from 0-1, where 0 is the beginning and 1 is the end. Messages are sent out the corresponding outlets in the same rhythm and at the same speed they were recorded.In other inlets: Starts playback of all messages on the track that corresponds to the inlet. Playback stars at a specific point, which is specified in a normalized range from 0-1.

messages.name: playatms
messages.digest: Start playback at a specific point - milliseconds
messages.description: In left inlet: Starts playback of all messages at a specific point, which is specified in milliseconds. Messages are sent out the corresponding outlets in the same rhythm and at the same speed they were recorded.In other inlets: Starts playback of all messages on the track that corresponds to the inlet. Playback stars at a specific point, which is specified in milliseconds.

messages.name: read
messages.digest: Load a savedfile
messages.description: In left inlet: Calls up the standard Open Document dialog box, so that a previously saved file can be read into. Only .txt, .pat, and .json files can be loaded.In other inlets: Opens a file containing only the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: record
messages.digest: Start recording
messages.description: In left inlet: Begins recording all messages received in the other inlets. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, begins recording those tracks.In other inlets: Begins recording messages on the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: rewind
messages.digest: Return to the start of the sequence/track
messages.description: In left inlet: Resetsto the beginning of its recorded sequence. This command is used to return to the beginning of the sequence when stepping through messages with. To return to the beginning of a sequence while playing or recording, just repeat theormessage. Whenis playing or recording, amessage should precede amessage. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, returns to the beginning of those tracks.In other inlets: Returns the pointer to the beginning of the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: stop
messages.digest: Stop recording or playback
messages.description: In left inlet: Stopswhen it is recording or playing. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, stops those tracks.In other inlets: Stops the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: timescale
messages.digest: Sets the timescale of a track
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the timescale for all tracks. 100 is the original timescale, whereas 200 would be twice as fast. This message can be set while a track is playing. Please note that when a track is played again, the timescale is reset to 100. For this reason, use of this message is strongly discouraged in favor of theattribute, which does not reset.In other inlets: Sets the timescale for the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: touch
messages.digest: Touch automation recording for a specific inlet
messages.description: Turn touch automation recording off/on for the track that corresponds to the inlet. Sending the message "touch 1" to a specific inlet while a track is playing, overwrites the existing recording with new data received in the track’s inlet. Timing is unaffected. Sending the message "touch 0" to a specific inlet ends the touch automation recording, and any events from that point on in the track play as usual. Themessage only works when a track is already playing.This message is for individual track inlets. To enable/disable touch automation recording on multiple tracks at once, use theandmessages, which are sent to the left inlet of.

messages.name: touchdisable
messages.digest: Disable touch automation recording
messages.description: In left inlet: Turns touch automation recording off for the specified tracks. Sending the message "touchdisable 2 3" ends touch automation recording on tracks 2 and 3. Any events from that point on in the tracks play as usual. This message is used in conjunction with themessage. Timing is unaffected. Themessage only works when a track is already playing.

messages.name: touchenable
messages.digest: Enable touch automation recording
messages.description: In left inlet: Turns touch automation recording on for the specified tracks. Sending the message "touchenable 2 3" while a track is playing, overwrites the existing recording for tracks 2 and 3 with new data received in the tracks' inlets. Use the messageto stop touch automation recording. Timing is unaffected. Themessage only works when a track is already playing.

messages.name: unmute
messages.digest: Unmute output
messages.description: In left inlet: Undoes any previously receivedmessages. The word, followed by one or more track numbers, unmutes those tracks.In other inlets: Unmutes the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write the sequence to disk
messages.description: In left inlet: Calls up the standard Save As dialog box, allowing the contents ofto be saved as a separate file. If the specified filename (given as an argument) ends in .json, a JSON format file is saved.In other inlets: Writes a file containing only the track that corresponds to the inlet.

messages.name: writejson
messages.digest: Write the sequence to disk in JSON format
messages.description: In left inlet: Calls up the standard Save As dialog box, allowing the contents ofto be saved as a separate file, in JSON format. Unlike themessage,writes times as floats, preserving the timing of events precisely.In other inlets: Writes a file, in JSON format, containing only the track that corresponds to the inlet.

outlets.digest: next Outputs list with Track and Duration
